problem.text: Global-scale estimation repeated the same tile for every inner-loop iteration: its column index used the fixed sampling width instead of the loop variable.

reasoning.text: Using w selects neighboring wrapped diagonals rather than duplicating one diagonal, increasing sample diversity without increasing the number of sampled tiles.

impact.text: The changed sample can change the selected global scale and subsequent quantization. Improved model quality or conversion speed is not established.

source_notes.text: The earlier multi-GPU entry records premature scale-search progress completion. Inspection of this patch shows that its arithmetic persists despite the new optional-progress guard.

The inspected discussions report an undefined __cxa_call_terminate symbol (#7), incoherent cogito output at bpw <= 2.5 (#15), a CUDA invalid-configuration error (#16), and missing torch during installation (#17). They do not establish that this sampling patch resolves those reports.

limitations: No PyTorch, CUDA kernel, or end-to-end conversion was executed. Scalar checks establish indexing and interval arithmetic only, not GPU numerical behavior or model quality.
The sampling comment hopes for representative coverage; neither representative distributions nor a unimodal scale-error objective were empirically established.

claims.text: g_scale_gss samples 16-by-16 tiles, flattens each to 256 elements, applies tensor_core_perm, and stacks them for trial quantization. With default width 3, the corrected column index ((i + w) % tiles_n) spans three wrapped offsets per i; the old index repeated ((i + 3) % tiles_n) three times. Modulo wrapping can still produce duplicates when the tile grid is narrow.

A scalar transcription confirmed unchanged sample counts but greater distinct coverage: a 4-by-4 tile grid has 12 samples and changes from 4 to 12 unique tiles; a 2-by-5 grid changes from 5 to 10 unique tiles among 15 samples.

Each trial quantizes tiles multiplied by scale, divides reconstructed values by that scale, and minimizes mean squared error against the original samples. Golden-section search retains bounds 0.1 and 1.9 and stops when interval width is at most 0.01; these are scale-search parameters, not bitrate limits.

The whole-parent caller search found one direct caller, quantize_exl3. It supplies a ProgressBar after channel normalization and Hadamard transforms, multiplies weight_r by the returned scale, and divides su by the same scale before LDLQ. This compensating adjustment preserves the reconstruction scaling convention while changing the values presented to quantization.

The patch also suppresses verbose interval-by-interval printing while retaining the final scale/error message, and guards pb.update so the default pb=None no longer causes an attribute access there. The newly appended synchronization loop follows an unconditional return and is unreachable on normal completion.

findings.description: The newly added exit synchronization cannot execute.
findings.expected_behavior: If the added loop is intended to synchronize selected devices before returning, it must run before the return.
findings.actual_behavior: return best_scale exits inside the stream context before control can reach the appended device loop.

verification.description: Compared the appended loop with the unconditional return and inspected quantize_exl3, the only direct caller found in the whole-parent search.
verification.limits: This establishes dead code, not a CUDA race or a requirement for additional synchronization.

findings.description: The optional-progress guard carries over the premature-completion calculation.
findings.trigger: g_scale_gss contracts its interval with a visible ProgressBar supplied by quantize_exl3.
findings.expected_behavior: Intermediate search progress should remain distinguishable from completion.
findings.actual_behavior: int(delta2 / delta1) becomes zero after the first contraction, so every loop update reports 100 even while search continues.

verification.description: The sole located direct caller supplies a progress object; ProgressBar.update forwards the number as completed work. The patch guards the update but leaves its expression unchanged.
verification.limits: Visibility depends on the caller supplying progress text; terminal rendering was not executed.

verification.description: Modeled golden-section contraction from interval width 1.8 to below 0.01: all 11 updates were 100, ending at approximately 0.009045.
verification.limits: Standard-library arithmetic only; not execution of the repository search or CUDA objective.

annotation.summary: Corrects global-scale tile sampling to use distinct wrapped offsets, guards optional progress updates, and reduces verbose output. Premature progress completion persists, and newly appended synchronization is unreachable.

for k,n,w in [(4,4,3),(2,5,3),(4,2,3)]:
 old=[(i%k,(i+w)%n) for i in range(max(k,n)) for j in range(w)]
 new=[(i%k,(i+j)%n) for i in range(max(k,n)) for j in range(w)]
 print((k,n,w),'samples',len(new),'unique old/new',len(set(old)),len(set(new)))
d=1.8; updates=[]
while d>0.01:
 d*= (math.sqrt(5)-1)/2
 updates.append(100-100*int(d/1.8))
print('iterations',len(updates),'updates',updates,'final width',d)
